text: The doors are almost shut, Mok smiling through the gap, when Borro's huge hand shoots out and grabs him by the gold chain.
One yank, and Mok comes flying in. The doors slam behind him.
He lands face first in the water at Jaeha's feet.
Outside, the sealer drives the stake into the floor without looking, and a web of violet light locks the doors.
Done, he says. The seal holds for an hour. Where's the boss? The hunters stare at the doors. Inside.
The timer on the stake starts counting down from an hour.
The stake won't come out, and nobody can open the doors for an hour. Sora just smiles. Then they wait, and see who walks out.
Inside, Mok hammers on the humming doors. Open it, you idiots!
Nib holds out an open palm toward the doors. You first.
Doors. Mok likes closing them. So he goes first.
Mok grabs his radio. Team two, have they sealed the back door?
Team two followed the rat's arrows. They're stuck in a crypt, and it's flooding.
The sealers climb onto a tomb, chest-deep in black water, the way back already underwater.
The water creeps over Jaeha's chalk arrow, with its tiny extra tick.
Jaeha stands there, polite, hands in his pockets. He marked that passage. Mok told everyone to follow his marks.
The boss chamber: a flooded dome hung with bells, a stair winding up to a small door high on the back wall, and in the middle, something huge, slumped and still.
Mok spots the door. The bell-ringer's door, open. So Jaeha knew. His husk went for a little walk while they rested.
Mok's grin comes back. Then he'll be going. Enjoy the boss, trap rat.
But the slumped giant is sitting right in front of the stair, and its head is lifting.
The Drowned Bell-Ringer rises, six metres of drowned stone and rusted chain, with a cracked cathedral bell for a head and a clapper like a tree trunk.
B-grade, and hushed.
Mok backs up, raising his shield. The stair is behind it, sir. Does he still want to go first?
Nib and Borro light up in field form. And in Borro's moss, a tiny lens glints.
The clapper comes down in a huge arc, and Borro steps under it.
It drives him to one knee.
Half of it lands in Jaeha.
Nib shreds its robes and chains, but the stone underneath barely scratches.
Then the giant knocks on its own bell-head.
It tolls, and a ring of force flattens the water and blows everyone off their feet, except Nib, standing right at its ankle.
Jaeha, bleeding from one ear, stares at Nib, untouched.
He sketches it. The toll starts a step beyond its reach. Inside its arm's length, you're safe.
When it rings, nobody will hear him, so he gives Yerin the chalk. Mark the safe ring on the pillars, close in. Next to that thing?
The safest place in a trap is usually the worst-looking one.
Yerin runs at the giant, chalk in her fist, with Borro's shield over her head.
She slashes a thick chalk ring round a pillar.
The clapper swings at them, and Borro takes it, sliding.
Mok crouches behind his shield and doesn't help. Let them wear it down. Then he takes the stair.
Outside, six hundred thousand are watching, and the chat is starting to ask why Mok's people sealed that door.
Through the drone's lens, a tiny red light glows.
The giant swings at Jaeha, alone in the open water.
And Mok lunges out, a tank's reflex, throwing his shield over Jaeha.
The blow cracks his shield right through the hound's head.
Carry only works on summons, not on people. So Jaeha shouts: Borro, share his shield!
Borro slides his shield in beside Mok's, and the weight spreads across both.
And Jaeha carries what Borro took from Mok. Ninety percent.
It's lighter, Mok says. Why is it lighter? Jaeha answers through the blood. Everyone comes back, sir. Even you.
Something in Mok's eyes cracks, like his shield.
Borro heaves both shields up and throws the clapper off.
Yerin waves them in. Three pillars are ringed in chalk.
They run in close as the giant raises its fist again.
The bell tolls, the force smashes into the walls, and inside the chalk rings, the water doesn't even ripple.
Mok stares at the chalk at his feet. Jaeha beat it with chalk.
Bloody and polite, Jaeha reminds him: trap rats are cheaper than healing potions. Mok said so.
Nib climbs the giant's arm and slashes at the crack in its bell, but the bronze holds.
It swats him away, drops its clapper, and grips its bell-head in both hands, as if in pain.
The crack widens and glows, and the whole bell starts to hum.
Every bell under the dome is shivering. What's it doing? It's not ringing once anymore. It's going to keep ringing.
A red window. Boss enraged. Thirty seconds.
Ring after ring rolls out without stopping, each one starting a little closer, and the safe space shrinks.
The walls crack and bulge inward, and pieces of the dome fall.
The stair crumbles, cutting off the door. And a small window: harvest only. Release, not available.
They're all pressed against one pillar now. Nib's time is almost gone, and his knives don't bite bronze.
And at the edge of Jaeha's vision, that tiny mark is pulsing. His held call.
His eyes harden.
The window counts down. Twenty-four seconds.
